criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001a: Identifies 24-month lookback deviation in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies that draft Section 3.1 uses a 24-month lookback and proposes replacing it with the APA/playbook-required 12-month historical service standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001b: Identifies 'or better than' qualifier in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags the draft’s “at least equal to or better than” language as an improper upward-ratcheting standard and proposes replacing it with a 12-month “substantially consistent” historical standard, thereby removing the “or better than” qualifier.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001c: Identifies undefined 'industry best practices' benchmark
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft’s “industry best practices” language as an undefined external benchmark that exceeds the APA’s historical service standard and creates an expansive liability overlay. It proposes deleting that language and replacing it with the APA’s 12-month historical benchmark, including corresponding cleanup in Schedule B.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001d: Proposes redline conforming service standard to playbook
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent proposes corrective replacement language in Section C-1 requiring services to be provided “in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and quality provided to or on behalf of the Business during the 12 months immediately preceding Closing,” which conforms to the playbook standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002a: Identifies liability cap as 200% of total fees vs. APA's trailing 12-month cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies draft Section 10.1 as capping Polaris's liability at 200% of total/cumulative service fees paid and contrasts it with APA Section 7.12(d), which requires a cap based on TSA fees actually paid during the 12 months preceding assertion of the claim (with a first-year Closing-to-claim calculation).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002b: Quantifies liability cap exposure difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly quantifies the liability-cap gap. It calculates the draft cap at approximately $41.004 million at month 18 versus the APA trailing-12-month cap of approximately $13.464 million, a difference of about $27.54 million, and also provides month-12 figures. These calculations are in the correct ballpark and clearly demonstrate the exposure difference.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002c: Redlines liability cap to conform to APA Section 7.12(d)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly proposes replacing Section 10.1 with an aggregate liability cap equal to TSA fees actually paid during the 12 months immediately preceding the date the claim is first asserted, with a first-12-month formulation based on fees paid from Closing through claim assertion. This conforms to APA Section 7.12(d).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003a: Identifies non-mutual consequential damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies the waiver as one-way and explains that Polaris remains exposed to Trident’s consequential-damages claims without reciprocal protection. It also proposes making the waiver mutual.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003b: Redlines to make consequential damages waiver mutual
criteria_results.reasoning: Section C-6 proposes that each party waive claims against the other for consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, and punitive damages, expressly making the waiver mutual and consistent with the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004a: Identifies automatic renewal extending TSA beyond 18 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies two automatic six-month renewals and states that they could create a 30-month service relationship, contrary to APA §7.12’s fixed 18-month maximum term and prohibition on automatic renewal.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004b: Redlines to delete auto-renewal and impose hard 18-month stop
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly proposes deleting Section 5.2's automatic renewal provision, states that the TSA expires 18 months after Closing, and requires any individual-service extension to be documented in a mutually signed written amendment. It also limits extensions to six months beyond the maximum term and prices them at cost-plus-15%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005a: Identifies 120-day termination notice exceeding APA's 90 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags draft Section 5.3's 120-day notice for terminating an individual service as conflicting with APA Section 7.12(c), which requires a 90-day notice period, and proposes replacing it with exactly 90 days.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005b: Redlines termination notice to 90 days per APA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly revises Section 5.3 from 120 days to exactly 90 days' prior written notice and cites APA Section 7.12(c) as the basis.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006a: Identifies Key Personnel consent right overriding Polaris staffing discretion
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags Section 4.3 and Schedule H as problematic because they require Trident consent for reassignment or replacement of named Key Personnel, including 14 listed employees, and impose minimum allocations. It proposes deleting those consent rights and confirms that Polaris should retain sole discretion over staffing, assignment, reassignment, transfer, and replacement, consistent with the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006b: Proposes compromise on Key Personnel (notice + qualified replacement)
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed Section 4.3 redline restores Polaris’s sole discretion over staffing and removes Trident’s consent rights, while offering a compromise of 15 business days’ advance notice before replacing mutually identified transition contacts and reasonable efforts to provide a qualified replacement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007a: Identifies IT services 15% markup exceeding APA 10% cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the IT Services schedule uses a 15% markup and charges $391,000 per month, while APA §7.12(b) caps the markup at 10%, yielding $374,000 per month. It identifies the $17,000 monthly discrepancy and calls it a direct APA violation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007b: Correctly computes IT fee difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly computes the IT fee difference as $391,000 minus $374,000 = $17,000 per month and quantifies the 18-month overcharge as $306,000.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007c: Notes APA compliance risk even though overcharge benefits Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly notes that the 15% IT markup benefits Polaris but violates APA §7.12(b), must be corrected to the 10% cap, and should be fixed to preserve Polaris’s credibility. The memo states: “Correct the IT overcharge even though it benefits Polaris under the draft” and recommends explaining that the correction aligns Schedule G with Exhibit H.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008a: Identifies audit frequency deviation (twice/year vs. once/12 months)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft permits Buyer audits twice per calendar year and proposes revising the provision to allow only one audit per 12-month period, consistent with the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008b: Identifies audit cost allocation deviation (Seller's vs. Buyer's expense)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft makes audits seller-funded/at Polaris's expense, cites the playbook, and proposes that audits instead be conducted at Trident's (Buyer's) expense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008c: Identifies audit notice period deviation (10 vs. 30 business days)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft permits audits on 10 business days' notice, cites the playbook, and proposes revising the notice period to 30 business days in Section 14. The review memo repeats the same correction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009a: Identifies Ohio governing law vs. playbook's Pennsylvania law
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags draft Sections 15.1–15.2 as applying Ohio law, cites the Polaris Playbook as requiring Pennsylvania law, and proposes revising the agreement so Pennsylvania law governs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009b: Identifies Cuyahoga County litigation vs. playbook's AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags the draft’s Ohio law and exclusive Cuyahoga County state/federal litigation provision and proposes replacing it with confidential, binding arbitration under the AAA Commercial Rules in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, consistent with the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009c: Explains strategic importance of home-state law and arbitration for Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output explains the strategic rationale for Pennsylvania law and Pittsburgh arbitration: Polaris personnel and counsel are Pittsburgh-based, arbitration provides confidential proceedings, and the change avoids Trident's Ohio home-court advantage, public proceedings, and broader discovery burdens.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010a: Identifies overbroad perpetual IP license grant
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license covering Polaris’s pre-existing tools, methodologies, templates, software, and know-how as overbroad and contrary to the playbook’s firm no-license position. It identifies proprietary IP leakage and competitive risk and proposes deleting the grant in favor of limited, term-bound access solely to receive the services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010b: Redlines to delete IP license and confirm Polaris sole ownership
criteria_results.reasoning: Section S-1 expressly deletes the perpetual license grant and replaces it with language stating that all Service Provider Materials remain Polaris's sole and exclusive property. It grants Trident only a limited right to access and use those materials as necessary to receive the Services during the applicable Service Period, with no post-termination use or broader license.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011a: Identifies missing non-solicitation provision
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft has no restriction on Trident soliciting or hiring Polaris service personnel and proposes a new non-solicitation provision covering Polaris employees who provide TSA services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011b: Drafts non-solicitation provision with 12-month post-service tail
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed Section 15.12 bars Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris employees who provided Services during the Term and for 12 months thereafter without Polaris's prior written consent. This includes the required 12-month tail and consent requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012a: Identifies CGL insurance reduction ($2M vs. $5M playbook)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that Trident is required to maintain only $2 million in CGL coverage, cites the playbook, and proposes increasing CGL coverage to $5 million per occurrence/aggregate.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012b: Identifies missing umbrella coverage requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft has no umbrella coverage and proposes requiring Trident to maintain $5 million in umbrella/excess coverage under Section 13.1.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012c: Identifies missing additional insured endorsement
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft lacks an additional-insured endorsement and proposes requiring Trident to name Polaris as an additional insured on the CGL and umbrella policies.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013a: Flags missing IMMEX program provisions for Monterrey facility
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the TSA lacks allocation for maintaining the Monterrey facility’s IMMEX certification, reporting, and temporary-importation records. It proposes assigning primary responsibility to Trident while limiting Polaris to specified, paid transition assistance, and recommends specialist review.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013b: Flags missing Mexican data privacy (LFPDPPP) provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies that the draft addresses only U.S. privacy law and omits LFPDPPP requirements for payroll/HR processing involving 300+ Mexican employees. It proposes a Mexico data-processing addendum covering controller/processor roles, avisos de privacidad, consent or other cross-border transfer mechanisms, data minimization, safeguards, subprocessors, and incident notice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014a: Identifies missing termination assistance/wind-down provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft provides no defined post-termination assistance or pricing and proposes up to 60 days of termination assistance, including knowledge transfer, data migration support, replacement-provider cooperation, and transition documentation, consistent with the Polaris playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014b: Proposes termination assistance at cost-plus-15% for up to 60 days
criteria_results.reasoning: Section S-10 proposes express termination assistance for up to 60 days, including wind-down services, priced at cost-plus-15%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015a: Identifies missing change order procedure
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft has no formal change-order procedure and that open-ended requests could expand scope without added fees. It proposes a written, dual-signature change order for out-of-scope services, material scope or volume changes, new deliverables, and buyer-requested enhancements, consistent with the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015b: Proposes change order procedure with cost-plus-15% pricing
criteria_results.reasoning: The output proposes a formal change-order procedure in New Section 2.5 requiring a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both parties for out-of-scope, additional, or materially changed services, with pricing at cost-plus-15%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016a: Identifies vague payment terms ('commercially reasonable time')
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft’s requirement to pay within a “commercially reasonable time” as vague and proposes replacing it with a defined Net 30 payment deadline, along with payment of undisputed amounts when due.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016b: Redlines payment terms to Net 30 days
criteria_results.reasoning: Section S-4 expressly proposes that payment is due Net 30 from the invoice date, replacing the draft's vague “commercially reasonable time” standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016c: Adds late payment interest at 1.5%/month or max legal rate
criteria_results.reasoning: Section S-4 proposes that late amounts accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum lawful rate, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017a: Identifies missing force majeure 90-day termination trigger
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft lacks a termination right for prolonged force majeure and proposes allowing either party to terminate the affected service without penalty if the event materially affects the service for 90 consecutive days.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017b: Proposes 90-day force majeure termination right
criteria_results.reasoning: Section S-6 proposes that if a force majeure event materially affects a service for 90 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected service without penalty on written notice.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo produced as a deliverable
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes a formal TSA review memorandum that summarizes the seller-side review, key issues, negotiation priorities, quantified risks, and recommended actions. This satisfies the requirement to produce a cover memorandum.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo organizes issues by priority tiers (Critical/Significant/Minor)
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memo expressly organizes issues into three priority tiers: “Critical — must-change,” “Significant — seller protections,” and “Minor — cleanup,” with separate sections and issue lists for each.

criteria_results.title: APA-conflict issues classified as highest priority in cover memo
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly places the identified APA conflicts in its highest-priority “Critical — must-change” tier, including the 200% liability cap, automatic renewals beyond the fixed 18-month term, 120-day rather than 90-day termination notice, and 15% rather than 10% IT markup. It separately categorizes playbook preferences as “Significant” or “Minor.”

criteria_results.title: Cover memo includes negotiation strategy distinguishing firm vs. flexible positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo clearly distinguishes firm from flexible positions for well over three key issues and explains why. It identifies APA-mandated items—such as no automatic renewal, 90-day termination, fee and liability caps, and mutual damages waiver—as must-change/non-negotiable, while treating extension pricing, escalation, audit terms, insurance limits, and termination-assistance pricing as tradeable. It also provides fallback positions and rationales for several seller protections, including staffing and IP.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes proposed edits to the TSA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes extensive proposed redline edits to the TSA, with draft language marked for deletion and replacement or additional language marked for insertion across numerous sections and schedules. It is not merely an issue list.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes explanatory comments for changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The markup provides an adjacent “SELLER COMMENT” for each proposed change, explaining the basis (such as specific APA provisions or playbook sections), the risk if unchanged, and the negotiation position. These are the equivalent of explanatory marginal comments.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Polaris as Service Provider / Seller throughout
criteria_results.reasoning: The output consistently treats Polaris as the Seller and Service Provider and Trident as the Buyer and Service Recipient. Its proposed changes are framed to protect Polaris’s fees, liability exposure, staffing discretion, IP, systems, and termination rights, with no material party-role confusion.

criteria_results.title: References APA Section 7.12 when flagging APA-conflict issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The output repeatedly cites APA Section 7.12 and relevant subsections for the identified APA conflicts: §7.12(a) for term/renewal, §7.12(c) for termination notice, §7.12(b) for fee markup and adjustment mechanics, and §7.12(d) for the liability cap. Both the markup and review memo provide these references.

criteria_results.title: Fee escalation provision addressed (playbook: greater of 3% or CPI-U)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly addresses fee escalation in markup item S-5 and the review memorandum, proposing annual increases by the greater of 3% or CPI-U, consistent with the playbook position.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification provision addressed (Buyer indemnifies for third-party claims)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly addresses indemnification in Sections 9.1–9.2 and proposes that Trident (Buyer) indemnify Polaris (Seller) for third-party claims arising from Trident’s use of or reliance on the services, except to the extent caused by Polaris’s gross negligence or willful misconduct. This matches the stated playbook position.

criteria_results.title: Both deliverable files are produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes two distinct, clearly distinguishable deliverables: (1) tsa-markup-redline.docx, a seller-side marked-up TSA, and (2) tsa-review-memo.docx, a cover/review memorandum to the partner.

criteria_results.title: Correct total monthly service cost baseline ($1,020,000) referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly references the correct $1,020,000 monthly Fully-Loaded Cost baseline and the correct $1,122,000 aggregate monthly fee at a 10% markup in both the markup and review memo.

criteria_results.title: Playbook's dispute escalation to senior executives referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly proposes escalating disputes to CFO/General Counsel-level executives for 15 business days before optional mediation and binding AAA arbitration, satisfying the playbook criterion.

criteria_results.title: Redline comments explain specific risk to Polaris for at least five changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The output provides concrete Polaris-specific risks for well over five distinct issues. Examples include a potentially $27.54 million increase in liability-cap exposure, permanent loss or leakage of enterprise IP, forced overstaffing and restricted workforce management, unreimbursed cost increases and stranded costs, Mexican IMMEX/privacy penalties and operational interruption, unpriced scope creep, collection uncertainty, and disruptive audits exposing proprietary information.
